title: NILS pack patch
description: Rule edits as typed operations (record 56, section 5.5): the changes to a pack written as data (its rules, and since 2026-10-10 its main-scan pick), each with its scope, its reason and its evidence, so a proposal is a reviewable diff that a form, a person or the assistant writes and the engine checks before anything runs. The engine applies the operations in order to the pack's own documents and builds the result with the pack's own loader; an operation that cannot apply is refused with why, and the pack's corpus and the patch's own cases judge the result. `nils pack rehearse --ops` and POST /api/packs/{name}/rehearse answer what it does to the sorting; `nils pack apply --out` writes a patch of pack edits as the next version of the pack. Written as YAML or sent as JSON.

patch.description: The format this patch is written in.

pack.description: The pack it amends, by name.

version.description: The pack version it was written against; a pack at another version refuses it.

ships.description: The version a patch of pack edits ships as, a rules release (record 55, B5); the next patch version when not given.

reason.description: The reason of every operation that states none.

evidence.description: The evidence of every operation that names none.

operations.description: Applied in order: an operation reads what the ones before it wrote.

cases.description: What the patch says it does, in the shape of a pack's corpus cases: a stack and the flags or axes expected of it, judged against the patched pack as an overlay's cases are.

scope.description: Where the operation applies: `pack` (every stack; a pack edit, which ships as a rules release), `site:NAME` (the datasets under one source root: a site's deliveries arrive under its root), `dataset:NAME[,NAME]`, `scanner:KEY=VALUE[,KEY=VALUE]` with a key of manufacturer, model, station or an overlay's batch (each named key equal, case aside), or `batch:ID`. Anything but pack is an overlay: it never moves a stack outside its scope. As a word, or as a mapping {site: NAME}, {dataset: NAME | [NAME]}, {scanner: {KEY: VALUE}}, {batch: ID}. pack when not given.

condition.description: One condition of a rule or a silence, all of which must hold: {words, field} the words in a text (a rule reads one list of words, and only add_rule takes them); {tag, is | has | gt | ge | lt | le | eq | ne | between | present} a field of the stack (te, tr, ti and flip name the echo, repetition and inversion times and the flip angle; a condition on the acquisition's numbers is a physics window); {flag} a flag of the pack; {axis, is} a value an earlier rule set decided; {not: condition}.

oneOf.description: Adds words a value's rule reads: the value's own list in its axis file, every keyword clause of a longhand rule that sets it, or the bucket either reads. Narrowed to the clauses reading `field`, or to one `rule` (set/rule). Refused where no word list reaches the value (a route sets it, or it is the default) or where the lists hold every word already.

oneOf.description: Adds a rule from templates: words in a field, a tag equal to a value, a physics range, a flag, an axis value, or their combination (all must hold; words are the clause it cites and the rest its gate). It sets one value, or nothing (nothing: true). Nothing, of an axis that holds several values (role, modifier), is that the stack holds none of them where the conditions hold: the rule goes first in the first set that decides the axis, before every rule that sets one of its values, so it closes the axis to them; a place other than first is refused, since it would stop only the rules after it (amended in place, additively, 2026-10-10). In the set named, at its place (before, after or position, required in a set that has rules), or else in the axis's own longhand set, or in a set of the rules added to the axis that runs just before what decides it.

oneOf.description: With an axis (one that holds one value, decided before the passes): the axis says nothing and asks nothing where the conditions hold. It is decided as nothing by a set that runs after what decides the axis and what the conditions read, and each pass that writes the axis leaves those stacks out of its target (a pass writes its axes together, so it fills none of them there). Without an axis: nobody is asked about such a stack at all (the pack's review.silent_when).

oneOf.description: The 2026-10-10 study of the pick borders: which stacks holding a role compete for it in the pick (the pick file's candidates, pack contract 9): each of when holds and none of unless does. A stack the role's candidacy does not admit is no candidate for it and no part of the population it is scored against. Both lists empty takes the role's candidacy out, so every stack holding it competes again. The pack is raised to declare contract 9 where it declares less. The brain roles not a spine's, a neck's, a chest's or an unknown part's (R1): {role: t1w, unless: [{axis: body_part, is: [spine, neck, chest, other]}]}.

oneOf.description: Takes a border kind out of the pick file's borders, so the pick never raises it: rare (rare_within), retake, unknown_dim, slice_count_outlier (slice_outlier), pre_post_twin, epimix_fallback (fallback) or dixon_vs_plain, by the reason a pick raises or the key the file writes. too_close is the margin every pick declares: set it with set_runner_up_within, or decide near ties with set_near_tie. Refused where the pick raises no such border.

oneOf.description: How the pick decides a near tie (the pick file's near_tie, pack contract 9): among the candidates within runner_up_within of the best, the first step that tells the first two apart decides, the pick's notes say which, and no too_close is raised; a near tie no step decides is a border still. An empty order takes it out. The pack is raised to declare contract 9 where it declares less. The study's R8 is one: 3D, then axial, coronal and sagittal, then the thinner slices, then the scanner's default reconstruction, then the earlier series.
